description: Address and place-search expectations for the Azores (PT-20), for the shared runtime work (#31), grown from the Portugal proposal (#297), the Madeira pilot (#420) and its fixtures (#451). The twelve rows are verbatim rows of the live PT-20 index — the INE address register via the 2026-02-23 OpenAddresses upload — chosen to cover both INE island groups (AC25 Corvo and Flores, AC26 the rest, at least one eastern island) and the shapes an Azores query takes; tools/build_region_pt_20.py check covers the live index.

index_contract.table: addr(num TEXT, street TEXT, norm TEXT, city TEXT, state TEXT, zip TEXT, lat REAL, lon REAL, district TEXT)

meta.source: Instituto Nacional de Estatística, I.P., via OpenAddresses (CC BY 4.0)

rules: num is the register's house label with leading zeros stripped only when the rest is all digits ('007' becomes '7'; '0E', '2A' and '38 40' stay as written)
city is the INE locality as the register spells it, upper case, sometimes with a municipality suffix ('RIBEIRINHA AGH', 'LAGOA (SÃO MIGUEL)'), occasionally empty
state is PT-20 in every row; the district column is empty (the register has no district)
zip is the PT postcode NNNN-NNN stored without the hyphen
the index is a sidecar: map-set.json does not list it, as for the US state indexes

runtime_requirements: An index whose meta says norm = pt-1 is searched only with that rule, and US indexes (no norm key) only with the US rule.
With PT-20.sqlite installed, every answer from an existing US index stays identical, including its Overture Maps credit.
A PT address is written street first (LG VIGIA 61), so a result names the house street first, keeps the register's spelling, and credits the index meta source.
Only an exact house label matches: the house 2 never answers for the 2A beside it, 2A never answers for 2, and a 5 on street 1 never answers a query for street 2.
A label that is not a plain numeral ('2A') is kept and matched in either case, so '2a' finds '2A'.
The postcode is stored without the hyphen; a query types 9700-026, so the lookup strips the punctuation before comparing, as the US rule does.

The detail line is the US join over what the row holds (city, PT-20, zip) — the register's city in its own spelling, upper case, sometimes with a municipality suffix ('RIBEIRINHA AGH', 'LAGOA (SÃO MIGUEL)'), occasionally empty.
